comparison: Perfect agreement on validation of knock-in cell lines (C11-C15). Both evaluations find the validation methods (western blot, co-IP, luciferase, confocal imaging) convincing and support the functional tagging approach without concerns.

Complete agreement on baseline SMT measurements (C16-C20). Both evaluations accept the quantitative measurements, reproducibility across clones, and bimodal diffusion behavior. Peer reviewers specifically praised the state-of-the-art single-molecule microscopy approach.

Full agreement on ligand treatment findings (C21-C22). Both evaluations accept that atRA treatment does not significantly change fbound, consistent with ligand-independent chromatin binding for T2NRs. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Strong agreement on overexpression experiments (C24-C29). Both evaluations support the finding that RAR overexpression but not RXR overexpression increases fbound, with OpenEval covering C23 additionally. Peer reviewers explicitly noted this contradicts the prevailing model.

Agreement on RAR overexpression effects (C30-C34), though peer result R5 also covers RXR overexpression claims (C35-C38) that OpenEval separates into R6. Both evaluations strongly support these central findings showing RAR is limiting, not RXR. Peer reviewers called the evidence 'compelling.'

Overlap on RXR overexpression findings (C35-C39). OpenEval notes the interpretation relies on indirect inference about unmeasured RXR isoforms and partners, while peer reviewers accepted the conclusions without challenge, finding the evidence compelling for the paradigm shift.

Strong agreement on PAPA-SMT results (C42-C47). Both evaluations strongly support the direct demonstration of RAR-RXR heterodimerization and chromatin binding correlation. Peer reviewers praised the cutting-edge combination of techniques, with peer R6 also covering C49.

Agreement on main conclusions (C48-C51, with peer R7 also covering C4-C5). OpenEval notes the conclusion relies on assumptions about unmeasured partners but finds it well-supported. Peer reviewers strongly endorsed this paradigm-shifting conclusion as 'compelling' and providing 'unexpected novel insights.'

Both address the main finding claims (C4-C5). OpenEval R17 evaluates these as background/rationale statements that are well-supported, while peer R7 evaluates them as part of the paradigm-shifting conclusion with strong endorsement.

Divergence in evaluation of fbound difference interpretations (C52-C54). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative explanations and unvalidated expression data. Peer reviewers accepted these interpretations without challenge, noting authors appropriately specified limitations.

Agreement on RXR excess model (C55-C57, with peer R10 also covering C39, C64). OpenEval finds the inference well-supported but notes reliance on assumptions. Peer reviewers endorsed the model, with Reviewer 1 explicitly supporting the inference about T2NR pool sizes determining chromatin binding.

Divergence on mechanistic explanations (C58-C60). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting C58 is supported but C59-C60 are speculative without distinguishing evidence. Peer reviewers accepted these observations and interpretations without challenge as part of the broader narrative.

Partial overlap on ligand treatment observations (C62-C63, with peer R9 also covering C58-C60). OpenEval finds C62-C63 supported but notes reliance on indirect inference. Peer reviewers accepted the findings without challenge.

Minor overlap on C63. OpenEval evaluates C62-C63 together as supported with caveats about indirect inference. Peer R8 groups C63 with other interpretations (C52-C54, C57) and accepts them without challenge.

Divergence on study limitations (C65-C66, with OpenEval R13 also covering C64). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative statements requiring validation. Peer reviewers accepted these caveats as appropriate acknowledgment of limitations, with Reviewer 2 satisfied with how authors qualified conclusions.
Minor overlap on C64. OpenEval groups C64 with limitations (C65-C66) and rates as UNCERTAIN. Peer R10 groups C64 with the endorsed RXR excess model (C39, C55-C56) and supports it.

Agreement on methodological contributions (C68-C69). Both evaluations strongly support the utility of SMT/PAPA-SMT approaches. OpenEval notes C69 applications remain speculative until demonstrated. Peer reviewers strongly endorsed the paradigm for dissecting regulatory networks, calling it of 'broad interest.'

OpenEval evaluates background/rationale claims (C1-C3) as supported, establishing context for the study. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focused on experimental findings rather than background statements.

OpenEval evaluates methodological quality control measures (C77-C78) regarding trajectory numbers and cell-to-cell variance as supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers did not specifically comment on these technical parameters.
